facts.statement: Rocasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus (meaning "General Roca lizard") is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod that lived in South America.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Rocasaurus is highly pneumatic, similar to its close relatives Neuquensaurus and Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: As in the closely-related saltasaurines Neuquensaurus and Saltasaurus, the skeleton of Rocasaurus is highly pneumatic.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000 within the Allen Formation, dating to the middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian (75 to 70 million years ago).
facts.quote: Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000, within the Allen Formation which is dated to be middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian in age (75 to 70 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous).

facts.statement: Fossils were collected between 1989 and 1994 from Salitral Moreno, located 25 km south of General Roca in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Between 1989 and 1994, expeditions of the National University of Comahue and the Carlos Ameghino Provincial Museum collected titanosaur fossils from the locality of Salitral Moreno, 25 km south of the city of General Roca in Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Leonardo Salgado and Claudia Azpilicueta formally described the species Rocasaurus muniozi in 2000.
facts.quote: In 2000, Leonardo Salgado and Claudia Azpilicueta described some of these remains as representing a new genus and species, Rocasaurus muniozi.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the discovery near General Roca, while the species name honors Juan Carlos Muñoz for his support of paleontological research.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to its discovery near General Roca and the species name honors Juan Carlos Muñoz, director of paleontology at the Carlos Ameghino Provincial Museum, for his support of paleontological research in the region.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically from 75 to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000, within the Allen Formation which is dated to be middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian in age (75 to 70 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous).

facts.statement: Rocasaurus lived in what is now northern Patagonia, Argentina, during the Late Cretaceous (approximately 75 to 70 million years ago).
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del Cretácico Superior (hace aproximadamente entre 75 y 70 millones de años) en lo que hoy es el norte de la Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus was a small sauropod reaching 8 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and weighing 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Fue un pequeño saurópodo de sólo 8 metros de largo, 3 de alto y 4 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus differs from other saltasaurines by having a wide ventral fossa divided by a thin longitudinal septum in anterior tail vertebrae, and by ilium and ischium morphology with notably developed ischial blades.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus se diferencia de otros saltasaurinos por la presencia de una fosa ventral ancha dividida por un delgado septo longitudinal en las vértebras caudales anteriores, así como por la morfología del ilion e isquion, con láminas isquiáticas notoriamente más desarrolladas.

facts.statement: The strongly procoelous tail vertebrae feature large lenticular pneumatic pores directed horizontally on the sides, with an oval-shaped inferior channel connected to the spongy interior bone.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola fuertemente procoelwe tienen grandes neumatoporos lenticulares y dirigidos horizontalmente en los lados, también el canal en la parte inferior, que tiene la forma de un hueco ovalado, parece estar conectado con el hueso esponjoso del interior de la vértebra.

facts.statement: Later researchers noted that sacral vertebrae are extremely pneumatic, even more so than in other titanosaurs, and that the limbs appear quite elongated, unlike the stout legs of Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: Investigadores posteriores señalaron que las vértebras sacras son extremadamente neumáticas, incluso más que en otros titanosáuridos y que las extremidades parecen bastante alargadas como en los titanosáuridos normales, muy diferentes de las patas rechonchas de Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus appears to be closely related to saltasaurid dinosaurs such as Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus.
facts.quote: It seems to be closely related to saltasaurid dinosaurs, like Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus is classified within the subfamily Saltasaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Saltasaurinae

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the locality of General Roca, located north of the salar.
facts.quote: El nombre del género hace referencia a la localidad de General Roca, ubicada al norte del salar.

facts.statement: The species name honors Juan Carlos Muñoz, head of the paleontology department at the "Carlos Ameghino" Museum.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a Juan Carlos Muñoz, jefe del departamento de paleontología del Museo "Carlos Ameghino".

facts.statement: The holotype MPCA-Pv 46 was found in the lower Allen Formation dating to the Campanian-Maastrichtian and consists of a juvenile skullless skeleton.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MPCA-Pv 46, fue encontrado en una capa de la Formación Allen inferior que data del Campaniano-Maastrichtiano. Consiste en un esqueleto sin cráneo de un animal joven.

facts.statement: The holotype includes two cervical vertebrae, three dorsal vertebrae, two sacral vertebrae, two mid-caudal vertebrae, both ilia, a left pubis, both ischia, and a left femur.
facts.quote: Incluye dos vértebras cervicales, tres vértebras dorsales, dos vértebras sacras, una vértebra caudal media, una vértebra caudal media más posterior, los dos huesos ilion, un pubis izquierdo, ambos isquiones y un fémur izquierdo.

facts.statement: Rocasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Rocasaurus have been found in the Allen Formation in northwestern Patagonia, specifically in the provinces of Río Negro and Neuquén.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus de la Formación Allen

facts.statement: Rocasaurus lived in a diverse ecosystem that included turtles, fish, crocodiles, birds, ornithopods, abelisaurids, and megaraptorial theropods.
facts.quote: Esta formación contiene una asociación faunística diversa que incluye tortugas, peces, cocodrilos, aves y otros dinosaurios como ornitópodos, abelisáuridos y megarraptóridos

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Rocasaurus died and was rapidly buried by sediment, leading to good preservation of articulated skeletons.
facts.quote: La disposición y preservación de los fósiles sugiere una rápida cobertura sedimentaria posterior a la muerte del animal

facts.statement: Studies of Rocasaurus tail vertebrae revealed extensive internal pneumatization with small cavities separated by bone trabeculae.
facts.quote: El estudio reveló una extensa neumatización interna, con presencia de estructuras tipo camellae (cavidades pequeñas separadas por trabéculas óseas)

facts.statement: Researchers identified possible pneumatic bone tissue (pneumosteum) in only two tail vertebrae, suggesting it is not a universal marker for air sac invasion in sauropods.
facts.quote: El tejido conocido como neumosteo (pneumosteum), propuesto como posible marcador histológico de la invasión de divertículos aéreos en huesos de dinosaurios, fue identificado con dudas sólo en dos vértebras

facts.statement: Rocasaurus is considered one of the titanosaurians with the highest degree of postcranial pneumatization, including the tail, sacral vertebrae, and possibly the pelvic girdle.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus ha sido considerado uno de los titanosaurios con mayor grado de neumatización postcraneal conocido, incluyendo elementos de la cola, las vértebras sacras y posiblemente los cinturones pélvicos

facts.statement: Rocasaurus was classified within the subfamily Saltasaurinae in the year 2000.
facts.quote: Rocasaurus se colocó en Saltasaurinae en 2000

facts.statement: Saltasaurians like Rocasaurus are found in the northwestern region of Argentina, specifically in the Allen Formation of Río Negro and Neuquén provinces.
facts.quote: En el noroeste , Provincia de Salta, con Saltasaurus de la Formación El Lecho y del norte de Patagonia, provincias del Río Negro y del Neuquén, de Neuquensaurus de la Formación Río Colorado y Rocasaurus de la Formación Allen

facts.statement: It is likely that saltasaurians like Rocasaurus originated after the fragmentation of Gondwana and the opening of the South Atlantic Ocean during the mid-Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El hecho de que los saltasaurinos se han colocado únicamente en la Argentina, se parece indicar que, probablemente, ellos tendrían su origen después de la fragmentación de Gondwana, y la apertura del Atlántico Sur, un acontecimiento que ocurre posiblemente a mediados del Cretácico

facts.statement: Recent research suggests there may be a sauropod taxon in the Allen Formation distinct from Rocasaurus, though this is currently only possible evidence.
facts.quote: providing possible evidence of presence of a sauropod taxon distinct from Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, Bonatitan, Menucocelsior and Rocasaurus in the Allen Formation

rejected.quote: This genus grew up to 8 m long, making it one of the smaller sauropods.
